name: Question 12
problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,4x+3⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=x+2y+1$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

*Hint: You're given that the fundamental vector product of $S$ with respect to its canonical parametrization is $||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||=\sqrt{6}.$*
worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that our surface $z=x+2y+1$ can be written using the dot product as 

$$
⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{\overset{~}{n}}=1,\,\text{or}\,⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨1,\,2,\,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{-\overset{~}{n}}=-1.
$$

Since we require an upward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is positive. This gives us the normal vector

$$
\overset{~}{n}=⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩.
$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $z=x+2y+1$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,-y,\,4x+3⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨x+2y+1,\,-y,\,4x+3⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(-x-2y-1+2y+4x+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(3x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(3x+2)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(3x+2)\cdot ||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(3x+2)\cdot \sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\cancel{\sqrt{6}}}(3x+2)\cdot \cancel{\sqrt{6}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3x+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(3x+2)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}(3x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =[y]_{0}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+2x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =1\cdot 10 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$
